input.question: How did the American Southern accent develop?
input.ground_truth: It's more the other way around, and relates to the question "When did American English break from British English?". At first American and British English were the same, but then British English developed into what it is today. American English has not changed as much, and is actually closer to British English of 200 years ago. American Southern has been even slower to change (because of the relative isolation of the speakers), and is even closer to British English of that time!

That’s kind of how the American Southern accent started! A long, long time ago, people from England moved to the southern part of the United States. At first, they all talked the same way, but over many, many years, they started changing how they spoke. They mixed their English with words from Native American and African languages. They also started making their own new words and ways of saying things.

Because they were far away from England and didn’t hear the old way as much, their way of talking became different from people in the North or in England. That’s how the Southern accent grew and became its own special way of talking!
